title: Genetic counseling
what: A genetics doctor looks at whether inherited conditions run in your family and what the risk is for you or your child. They explain genetic test results in plain words.
why: When planning a pregnancy, after unusual screening results, if inherited conditions run in the family, or if a child has developmental differences.
duration: the visit usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; genetic test results, if ordered, take from a few days to a few weeks
tell_doctor: Conditions in close relatives: parents, siblings, children
Any miscarriages or pregnancies that stopped developing
If you and your partner are related by blood
How far along you are, if pregnant
What tests have already been done

prepare.title: Family
prepare.text: Ask your relatives in advance: who had what, at what age, and what your grandparents died of.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Gather discharge papers, screening, ultrasound, and test results, yours and your child's.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down what you want to know. It is easy to forget at the visit.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
Notes on conditions in the family
steps: The doctor asks about you, your pregnancies, and your relatives' health
A family tree is drawn: who had which conditions
If needed, you or your child are examined
The doctor explains what the risk is and what it depends on
If needed, tests are offered, and the doctor explains what they will show
feel: The conversation can be hard. That is normal. Ask any questions
You usually make the decisions. The doctor only explains
after: If a test was ordered, the clinic will tell you when results are due
You usually come back for a follow-up with the results

faq.q: Why see a geneticist if everyone in my family is healthy?
faq.a: Doctors sometimes advise it when planning a pregnancy or after screening. A geneticist will help you understand the risk, and reassure you if it is low.
Usually not. Most often blood is taken from a vein, or a swab from inside the cheek.
It often helps. The doctor needs the history of both families. Check with the clinic.
